scenario: A translational oncology team studying glioblastoma performs the following experiment: Prior to running DESeq2, an analyst filters out genes with fewer than 10 counts across at least 4 samples (the smallest group size), reducing the total tested genes from 35,000 to 18,000. They collect samples and execute computational modeling.
question: Critique the methodology of this glioblastoma study. Identify any fatal methodological flaws, explain the underlying biological and statistical mechanisms, provide rigorous corrections, and establish whether reported biological claims are warranted.
ground_truth_rationale: Authoritative scientific rationale: Standard rigorous practice: Pre-filtering low-count genes reduces the multiple-testing penalty in Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and removes uninformative high-noise Poisson background. In glioblastoma biology, failing to account for this leads to erroneous translational conclusions.
